style: Intense, high-energy football under Marcelo Bielsa. Aggressive man-oriented pressing, vertical attacking and relentless work rate layered over Uruguay's traditional defensive grit and tactical fouling. Built around a powerful midfield and clinical forwards.
recent_form: Solid and competitive. Finished fourth in CONMEBOL qualifying with the best defensive record in the group (just 12 goals conceded in 18 matches), reflecting Bielsa's structure. A strong, well-drilled side with a blend of elite talent and depth.

key_players.name: Federico Valverde
key_players.note: Real Madrid box-to-box midfielder, the heartbeat of the side; pressing intensity, late runs and long-range shooting make him uniquely dangerous.

key_players.name: Ronald Araujo
key_players.note: Barcelona defender anchoring the back line with strength, pace and leadership.

key_players.name: Darwin Nunez
key_players.note: Al-Hilal striker and Uruguay's top qualifying scorer with five goals; relentless runner with explosive finishing when sharp.

key_players.name: Giorgian De Arrascaeta
key_players.note: Flamengo playmaker providing the creative link and final-third quality behind the strikers.

key_players.name: Manuel Ugarte
key_players.note: Manchester United ball-winner who shields the defense and powers Bielsa's press.

key_players.name: Fernando Muslera
key_players.note: Veteran returning from international retirement for a fifth World Cup; set to become Uruguay's most-capped World Cup player.

historical_news: Two-time World Champions (1930 as inaugural hosts, and 1950 in the 'Maracanazo' upset of Brazil), giants of early football history.
Reached the 2010 World Cup semifinals in South Africa, their best modern finish, led by Diego Forlan and Luis Suarez.
Luis Suarez's controversial deliberate handball against Ghana in 2010 remains one of the tournament's most infamous moments.
End of the legendary Suarez-Cavani era and a generational handover toward the Valverde-Nunez-Araujo core.
Marcelo Bielsa appointed in 2023 to modernize and re-energize the national team with his high-press philosophy.
Reached the 2024 Copa America semifinals, signaling renewed ambition under Bielsa.

media_sentiment.label: neutral
media_sentiment.summary: Cautiously positive; respected as a well-organized Bielsa side with elite individuals, but viewed as a dark horse rather than a favorite, with questions over attacking consistency.
